2. Task 1 — Web Browser Configuration (Google Chrome)

2.1 Installation / verification

Google Chrome was already installed. Verification via terminal and chrome://version.

  • Command: google-chrome --version
  • Result: Google Chrome 156.0.8078.47
  • Executable: /opt/google/chrome/google-chrome
  • OS: Linux x86_64

2.2 Steps performed

  1. Checked browser name and version on chrome://version.
  2. Examined available settings on chrome://settings/.
  3. Configured default search engine to Google.
  4. Reviewed download location settings.
  5. Configured startup: Open the New Tab page.
  6. Reviewed privacy and security settings.
  7. Configured user profile name to “Aruzhan”.
  8. Opened wikipedia.org, github.com, and example.com in separate tabs.

2.3 Configured settings

  • Default search engine → Google
  • Downloads → Show downloads when done = ON
  • On startup → Open the New Tab page
  • Privacy → Safety Check / Safe Browsing reviewed
  • Profile name → Aruzhan

3. Task 2 — Communication Application (Telegram Desktop)

3.1 Purpose and features

Telegram Desktop is a cross-platform messenger. Features: text messaging, voice/video calls, file sharing, channels/bots, Secret Chats, multi-device sync.

3.2 Version and compatibility

  • Downloaded from telegram.org (official Linux package)
  • Version: 7.4
  • Platform: Linux x86_64

3.3 Configuration

  • Language → English
  • Connection → Default (HTTP used)
  • Update automatically → ON
  • Install beta → OFF
  • Interface scale → 100%
  • Theme → Classic
